extracted.intended_audience: Applicants to NIH K08 Mentored Clinical Scientist Career Development Award (mentored clinical investigators preparing NIH K08 applications)
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and assembling a mentored K08 NIH career development (PA-16-191) application, including Project Summary, Research Strategy, candidate training/mentorship plan, human subject protections, inclusion reporting, resource sharing, authentication of reagents, and timelines/budgets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow funding opportunity (FOA) instructions and current sample formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Always follow your funding opportunity's instructions for application format. Although this application demonstrates good grantsmanship, time has passed since the grantee applied. The sample may not reflect the latest format or rules. NIAID posts new samples periodically: https://www.niaid.nih.gov/grants-contracts/sample-applications
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the FOA-specific application format, page limits, and required attachments; consult the latest FOA for updates rather than relying solely on older sample applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Summary/Abstract content
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Summary/Abstract should succinctly state the public health problem, the gap in knowledge, the overall approach (systems biology applied to cohort samples), the main research aims, and the practical implications of the work for the field and for candidate development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include significance (why the problem matters), explicit aims, methods overview, expected outcomes, and a short statement of the candidate's commitment and institutional support (protected time, space, mentorship).

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Narrative — public health relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Project Narrative must explain the public health relevance of the proposed research (e.g., how identifying predictors/mechanisms of malaria immunity will aid vaccine development).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write a brief lay-language statement that describes why the work matters to public health and potential beneficiaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims — clear, focused aims
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must present clear Specific Aims (in this sample: two main research aims: 1) determine immune parameters predictive of clinical and sterile immunity; 2) relate immune parameters to plasma ability to inhibit parasite invasion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State concrete, testable aims that directly address the gap articulated in the summary and that map to experiments and analyses in the Research Strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candidate information and goals for career development
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the candidate's commitment to a research career (e.g., holding 80% protected research time), existing qualifications, the training objectives (e.g., biostatistics and computational biology), and how the proposed project advances career goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a targeted training plan with milestones and describe protected effort, current position, and how the award will develop independence in the proposed field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentoring plan and institutional commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a comprehensive mentorship plan naming primary mentor(s), co-mentors, collaborators, and institutional support (laboratory/office space, equipment, protected time).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include mentor roles, specific training and supervision plans, frequency of meetings, and letters/documentation of institutional commitment to the candidate's career development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Strategy content and Rationale (Significance, Innovation, Approach)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Research Strategy must present significance and rationale, place the work in context of prior literature, articulate novelty and innovation, and provide a detailed approach for experiments and analyses (including hypotheses and expected outcomes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use literature to justify the approach; define expected results and alternative strategies; link experiments to aims and to potential translational impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigor of Experimental Design and Quality Control
rubrics_metrics.description: All experiments must include measures to ensure rigor and reproducibility: randomization of sample processing to minimize batch effects, processing time points from the same child together to allow intra-subject controls, thorough documentation of sample processing procedures, and public release of raw data and analysis scripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly describe randomization schemes, batch-effect mitigation, sample tracking, QC steps, and a plan for public deposition of raw data and scripts to permit reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical analysis and multiple testing correction
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan and describe statistical modeling approaches (e.g., multinomial outcomes for immune classes, Cox regression for time-to-event analyses), comparisons of machine learning algorithms and regression models, and correction for multiple testing (Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify model inputs (covariates such as age), validation approaches, formal comparisons of algorithm performance, and the method for controlling false discovery when testing many features (e.g., microarray/proteomic data).

rubrics_metrics.name: Power, sample size, and handling of exploratory analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge limitations of sample size and mark direct comparisons as exploratory when sample sizes are small; consider pathway-level analyses to increase explanatory power when gene-level differences are modest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe planned power analyses where possible, designate exploratory versus confirmatory analyses, and present contingency/statistical strategies to mitigate small-sample limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of standardized, validated assay protocols
rubrics_metrics.description: Functional assays (e.g., Growth Inhibition Assays, microscale hepatocyte invasion assays) should use well-established, standardized protocols and appropriate positive/negative controls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite established methods, describe assay endpoints (e.g., fluorescence microscopy detection of anti-PfCSP, percentage of exoerythrocytic forms), and specify purification steps (e.g., IgG purification for GIAs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Correlation of functional assay outputs with multi-parameter data
rubrics_metrics.description: Correlate parasite-inhibitory activity scores from functional assays with antigen-specific IgG reactivity intensities (from a 1,087-protein Pf microarray) and other measured parameters using stage-specific combinatorial correlation approaches and multiple-testing adjustment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the computational approach for correlating assay outputs with high-dimensional antigen reactivities and how significance will be assessed (including multiple-testing correction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of functional and omics data via modeling and validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Integrate inhibitory activity scores and Aim 1 parameters (including age) into predictive models whose outcomes are clinically immune, sterilely immune, or susceptible; compare ML algorithms and regression models and validate findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify modeling frameworks, feature selection/regularization approaches (e.g., elastic net referenced), cross-validation/validation datasets, and criteria for model selection and reporting performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of Human Subjects and IRB considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly state whether human subjects are involved, whether the project is exempt, provide exemption numbers if applicable, report IRB approval dates or pending status, and include Human Subject Assurance numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using existing coded biospecimens and data, document exemption status and that investigators cannot identify subjects; ensure IRB approvals both in U.S. and foreign sites for international fieldwork.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of women and minorities reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide PHS Inclusion Enrollment Report data reporting enrollment by sex and NIH-specified racial/ethnic categories, even when using existing datasets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the prescribed PHS format for reporting cumulative (actual) enrollment and specify whether the study uses existing resources; explain any deviations or special circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of children — justification and assent/consent
rubrics_metrics.description: If children are included, justify the age range (e.g., 6 months–12 years to capture period of immunity acquisition), state assent and parental consent procedures, and confirm that no additional risk occurs if only existing specimens are used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe assent procedures for capable minors (ages 7–18), parental consent, culturally appropriate consent adaptations (e.g., grandparent consent in local custom), and how age will be handled analytically (as a covariate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and resource sharing plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe plans for dissemination of materials and data consistent with institutional and NIH policies: e.g., raw sequence data to NCBI SRA, processed sequencing to GEO, Plasmodium sequences to EuPathDB/PlasmoDB, and public release of custom scripts at project end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify timelines for data deposition, any anticipated Material Transfer Agreements, venues for presentation, and publication/dissemination plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of key biological and chemical resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Authenticate and document sources for key reagents: type O+ human erythrocytes (source: Indiana Blood Center), authenticated Pf 3D7 blood-stage parasites (authenticated by 6-loci microsatellite genotyping), commercially sourced cryopreserved primary human hepatocytes and supporting cells, and vendor/source lists for antibodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide authentication methods (e.g., genotyping), vendor names, catalog/clones for critical antibodies and reagents, and ensure traceability of biological stocks used in assays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reagent and antibody specification and provenance
rubrics_metrics.description: List anticipated antibodies (markers, fluorochromes, clones, catalog numbers) and commercial vendors to ensure reproducibility and enable authentication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full reagent tables where appropriate, and update with lot numbers/validation data at experiment time; include anticipated panels for flow cytometry with clones and fluorochromes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample processing, randomization, and batching procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Randomize sample processing to ensure equal distribution of outcome classes, key covariates (e.g., age), and minimize batch effects; process timepoints from the same subject together to enable intra-subject comparisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document randomization algorithms, batching schedules, and how potential confounders are balanced across batches; retain metadata to adjust analytically for any residual batch effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated problems, limitations, and contingency plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly state likely problems (e.g., small sample sizes leading to exploratory comparisons, variability in plasma inhibitory activity) and propose mitigation strategies (e.g., pathways analysis to boost power, focus on individuals with extreme phenotypes for mechanistic follow-up).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be realistic about limitations, describe how findings will guide future studies, and provide contingencies for experimental/analytical challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities and Other Resources adequacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe institutional facilities, laboratory and support space, affiliated hospitals, and resources available to conduct the proposed work (e.g., IUSM lab space, partner institutions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include descriptions that demonstrate adequate space, equipment access, and institutional environment supportive of the candidate's success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and budget justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide itemized budget pages for each performance year and a clear budget justification for personnel, supplies, equipment, and other costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Align budgetary requests with the proposed work and institutional policies; include cumulative budget and justify key line items relative to experimental plan and training activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeline, deliverables, and future directions
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a program-year timeline showing planned laboratory/data generation, computational analysis, presentations/manuscripts, and R01 grant preparation across years 1–5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a year-by-year table of milestones and deliverables that aligns with aims and the candidate's transition to independence; indicate expected outputs (manuscripts, conferences, data deposition).

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR) training and oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Detail RCR training (e.g., CITI certificates in Good Clinical Practice, Responsible Conduct of Research, Human Subjects Research), planned enrollment in ethics courses/workshops, refresher frequency, and mentor oversight to ensure ethical compliance in domestic and international research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide course names, contact hours when relevant, frequency of refresher training, and describe mentor/institutional roles in ensuring IRB approvals and ethical conduct.
